newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up in volatile trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed up in volatile trade against the dollar on Wednesday, as speculators continued to trade heavily on fears that depreciation of the local currency may have ended, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.65 to the dollar, after opening at 58.68, climbing to 58.60 and falling back to 58.77, they said.
"The exchange rate moved in topsy-turvey fashion as banks unwound dollar positions while trying to minimise losses," said a Union Bank dealer.
The rupee began rising on Tuesday when banks began selling dollars in the belief that the Central Bank had reached its short-term depreciation targets, dealers said.

The Central Bank, which pushed the dollar down by three quarter local-cent on Wednesday and fixed buying and selling rates at 58.2095 and 59.3855, left the rate unchanged on Tuesday despite slight overseas gains by the greenback, they said.
"Sale of dollars slowed down towards the end as banks expect the Central Bank to push up the dollar on Thursday due to slight overseas gains," said a Hatton National Bank dealer.
The overnight call money market, which closed at 10 percent after opening at 10.5, was subdued compared to the forex market, dealers said.
